title: Characterisation of blood cell aggregates in sepsis using digital holographic microscopy
summary:
Bacterial, viral or fungal infection can lead to a life-threatening disease known as sepsis. The pathogens trigger a defense reaction in the body, which in some cases takes an uncontrolled course. If sepsis is not recognized and treated in time, it can lead to multiple organ failure and often results in death. Therefore, it is important to develop methods that enable an early diagnosis of the disease and detect patients at high risk for progressions at an early stage. 
Previous studies have been able to show that altered blood cells and cell aggregates circulate in the blood of septic patients. We have developed a method that allows to microscopically detect and analyze blood cells and cell aggregates without staining or preparation steps. In this study, we will assess blood cell aggregates in patients with suspected or early diagnosed sepsis. Further, we will measure messengers released from artificially stimulated blood cells of these patients and assess clinical parameters. We aim to develop markers that could enable earlier diagnosis and thus earlier targeted therapy in the future.

interventions.name: positive qSOFA score: Assessment of clinical, laborchemical and imaging data from the medical chart, assessment of blood cells and aggregates using digital holographic microscopy (DHM) and assessment of cell-specific cytokine responses using flow cytometry within 48h from positive qSOFA (t0), on day

healthy controls: Single assessment of blood cells and aggregates using digital holographic microscopy,  assessment of cell-specific cytokine responses using flow cytometry, assessment of basic demographic data.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
positive qSOFA (minimum two of three criteria: respiratory rate ≥ 22/min, GCS<15, systolic blood pressure ≤ 100 mmHg)

OR

healthy individuals
Exclusion criteria:
lack of consent
